title: 25-Layer Defect Cavity with Adjacent-Layer Delta Constraint (<=40 nm)
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining adjacent-layer thickness differences to <=40 nm will prevent abrupt optical impedance jumps that cause phase mismatch, enabling smoother chirp progression and recovering target scores above 0.95 while maintaining 25-layer manufacturability.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass filter with quarter-wave DBR mirrors surrounding half-wave defect cavity, with smooth thickness progression enforced through bounded adjacent-layer deltas in the chirp sweep region (layers 5-16).
proposed_topology: Air | (Ta2O5/SiO2)_5 | Ta2O5 (defect cavity) | (SiO2/Ta2O5)_5 | Fused Silica - exactly 21 finite coating layers total (10 pairs + 1 defect)
manufacturing_considerations: adjacent-layer thickness delta <= 40 nm constraint for deposition smoothness
quarter-wave initialization at 1550 nm for baseline
theory_basis: Defective DBR structure (HL)^N D(LH)^N creates transmission peak at defect mode wavelength
Smooth impedance gradients reduce scattering losses and maintain bandgap integrity
expected_advantages: Smoother thickness progression reduces phase mismatch
Delta constraint prevents optimizer from generating abrupt jumps
known_risks: Delta constraint may limit optimizer search space
21 layers may be insufficient for deep sideband suppression compared to 27-layer best
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR receiver. Stack sequence: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 (defect cavity) | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | Fused Silica. Initialize all high-index layers to 185 nm and low-index layers to 267 nm (quarter-wave at 1550 nm), except defect cavity at 534 nm (half-wave). Optimize all 21 layer thicknesses with bounds 50-400 nm for DBR layers and 400-650 nm for defect cavity. Enforce adjacent-layer thickness difference constraint: |d[i+1] - d[i]| <= 40 nm for layers 5 through 16. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized. Target: maximize mean transmittance in 1550+/-5 nm band, minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Implementing feedback directive to enforce adjacent-layer delta <= 40 nm and monotonic progression in chirp region (layers 5-16) to prevent abrupt optical path jumps causing phase mismatch. Returning to 21-layer count to test whether constraint alone recovers performance without increasing layer count.
